# feat: registry-message wiring in the template library (loader, extractor, system-host)

**Target repo:** intropy-templates (integrio-intropy/intropy-templates), with one
scoped optional touch on intropy-topology under T3. This plan lives in the CLI
repo because the CLI side has already shipped the contract these templates must
meet; the plan file stays untracked per the docs precedent.

## Overview

The CLI now wires messages end to end: `--subscribe`/`--publishes` resolve a
registry message, snapshot the channel into the scaffold record's blocks, and
assembly consumes the blocks offline. The template library cannot receive any
of it: loader and extractor lack the `message-params` label (both flags are
usage errors), their `topic` parameter still forces the hand-typed
half-contract dance, the skeletons render CloudEvent identity from a
topic-derived guess instead of the resolved message, and the system-host
template has no `messages` section at all — the CLI's payload `messages` key is
silently ignored on render. This plan makes the library a working counterpart
of the shipped CLI.

---

## Problem Frame

The CLI-side plans (docs/plans/2026-09-04-001-…, docs/plans/2026-09-04-002-…)
wired subscribe and publish against **fixture** templates built in tests —
"what the template PR will ship", as the fixture comment that shipped says.
Against the real library: `int create loader --subscribe <ref>` fails on the
message-parameters gate; `int create extractor --publishes <ref>` likewise;
and even where wiring would land, `Constants.cs` renders `EventType` from
`eventTypeValue` — a topic-derived guess (`<org>.<first>.<last>`) that the
registry's authoritative CloudEvents type exists to replace. The system-host
ignores the payload's `messages` list entirely, so a host render carries no
message definitions for `sys update`'s stored-window or future enrichment.

The CLI contract the templates meet (verified in the CLI repo):

- Manifest labels `intropy.io/block-kind` (direction: extractor publishes,
  loader subscribes, transactional wire no messages) and
  `intropy.io/message-params` (comma list of message parameter names; one
  parameter maximum under the flags).
- With a flag, the resolved `subscribe`/`publishes` block lands in values
  under its key — **additive to declared parameters**; skeletons can render
  from it without the keys being declared parameters.
- The flag seeds every message parameter with the resolved message id;
  `contract` is explicitly not resolved (transitional .NET, stays a
  parameter).
- Degradation: no registry → interactive runs warn and fall back; the pinned
  internal-message flow (topic-less producer on the system pubsub, topic =
  message name) still works — the template must not break it.

---

## Requirements Trace

(Referencing the CLI-side origin docs; R items here are plan-local.)

- T1. Loader and extractor declare `intropy.io/message-params` with a single
  optional `message` parameter; `int create loader --subscribe <ref>` and
  `int create extractor --publishes <ref>` scaffold fully without prompting
  for topic or event identity.
- T2. Skeletons render the resolved wiring with a defined precedence:
  registry snapshot block > explicit override parameters (`topic`,
  `eventType`, `eventSource`) > derivations (`eventTypeValue`) >
  convention (topic = message name).
- T3. system-host declares the optional `messages` payload parameter and
  renders the message registry; the graph verb's topology carries the
  messagegroups section for internal messages, omits externally-published
  ones, and the CLI round-trips it (already decodes a nil section).
- T4. Templates never derive `subscribe`/`publishes` keys in `spec.values`
  — the CLI (flag, or a hand edit) is the block writer.
- T5. Internal flows are unchanged in outcome: no flags, no registry →
  topic/contract prompts as today, topic-derived event type, and the
  topic-less-producer convention still assembles.

---

## Scope Boundaries

- No CLI changes (except the optional T4 guard noted under Open Questions —
  deliberately deferred to a CLI follow-up).
- No changes to deploy-component, deploy-host, shared-contracts, or the
  transactional template (transactional-integration wires no messages).
- No codegen of types from `dataschema` (an external tool's job, per the
  subscribe doc's A2) — the producer only records the pin.
- No changes to CloudEvent identity *defaults* for the flag-less flow.

---

## Context & Research (verified on template-repo main, ac434c3, tag v0.9.0)

- `extractor/template.yaml` — required `topic` + `contract`; labeled
  extractor/in; `values:` derives `eventTypeValue` from topic (`<org>.
  <first>.<last>`), `pubsub: 'pubsub'` hardcoded; **no** derived publish
  block.
- `loader/template.yaml` — same shape; `SubscriptionRoute = "/events/{{ .topic }}"`.
- `extractor/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` — renders `PubSubName` ("pubsub"
  literal), `TopicName` = `{{ .topic }}`, `EventSource`/`EventType` with the
  override-else-derive pattern already in place.
- `loader/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` — same pattern + `SubscriptionRoute`.
- `system-host/template.yaml` — payload parameters: name, topics, ports,
  components, sharedContracts. **No `messages`.**
- `system-host/skeleton/Topics.cs.tmpl` — ranges `.topics`, derives field
  names, renders `TopicRef<T>`; collisions fail the render loudly.
- `system-host/skeleton/Program.cs` — `graph` verb delegates to
  `IntropyGenerate.Run(assembly, args)` from **Intropy.Topology.Generation**;
  there is no messagegroup code anywhere in the skeleton, and no `MessageGroup`
  in the intropy-topology model (only Topics materialized from edges).
- CLI-side: `internal/system/assemble.go` aggregates internal publishes into
  `Model.Messages`; `payload.go` writes `{name, type, contract?, dataschema?,
  publisher?}`; `update.go` matches that shape; external publishes are
  excluded from both.

---

## Key Technical Decisions

- **One optional `message` parameter, not a rename of anything.** The
  message id is a distinct fact (CloudEvents type) from the topic; a new
  optional parameter plus a precedence rule is additive and keeps the
  flag-less flow byte-identical. Required-ness stays off the flag path:
  required parameters would force both the flag and a prompt.
- **Snapshot-first rendering precedence.** The block is the CLI-owned truth
  for channel and message; params remain the authoring surface for
  out-of-registry flows. `topic` becomes optional: present → prompted
  internal flow as today; absent with a block → block wins; absent with
  `message` (internal) → the CLI's convention (topic = message name) renders
  into Constants so a topic-less producer still builds a coherent record and
  render without the CLI changing.
- **The derived-block guard is a template-repo discipline, not code.** No
  template derives `subscribe`/`publishes` in `spec.values` (none does
  today); a CLI-side hard guard stays deferred (see Open Questions).
- **Messagegroups render from the payload `messages` inside the host, behind
  a clean seam.** The host skeleton renders the message registry from the
  `messages` payload; where the graph section is composed — Generation vs a
  host-side wrapper — is the fork under Open Questions, resolved during
  implementation by reading IntropyGenerate's discovery contract.
- **Versioning: `v0.10.0-rc.1`** before stable. Additive shapes, old records
  read unchanged; rc keeps CI current while the CLI pins settle.

---

## Open Questions

### Resolved During Planning

- Pan-template scope: only loader, extractor, system-host touch messaging.
  streaming-extractor/apiservice exist only on other branches — out of scope
  here, but T1's pattern applies when they land.
- The event-identity override parameters (`eventType`, `eventSource`) keep
  their slot in the precedence chain — they are the migration escape hatches
  the CLI resolution sits above, not competitors.

### Deferred to Implementation

- **T3 seam (Needs research):** where the topology `messagegroups` section is
  composed. Candidate (a) — extend Intropy.Topology's model + Generation
  composition, if discovery can see the rendered message registry; candidate
  (b) — the host's graph wrapper injects the section into the JSON it prints.
  Decide by reading `IntropyGenerate.Run`'s discovery contract; (b) is the
  smaller change but keeps the section out of the model that owns topology
  shape.
- **Injector shape:** what the skeleton's message registry artifact looks
  like (static class of typed message definitions vs data file) — decide
  against how Generation discovers inputs.
- Prompt UX for the optional `message` parameter on the no-flag path (offer?
  omit? registry pick list fires only when the parameter is required-pending
  — verify against CLI prompting, which works for any declared message
  parameter).

---

## Implementation Units

- [ ] T1. **Loader + extractor manifests: message parameter and label**

**Goal:** Both flags pass the CLI's gates against the real templates and seed
the correct values.

**Requirements:** T1, T5

**Dependencies:** None

**Files:**
- Modify: `loader/template.yaml`, `extractor/template.yaml`
- Test: template-repo test pattern (see Verification)

**Approach:**
- Add `intropy.io/message-params: message`.
- Add optional `message` parameter (string; dotted pattern for a CloudEvents
  type, e.g. `^[a-z0-9]+([.-][a-z0-9]+)*$`); description states it is seeded
  by `--subscribe`/`--publishes` or picked from the registry, and that event
  identity prefers it over the topic-derived default.
- Make `topic` optional in both manifests. The extractor's topic doc loses
  "scaffold the consuming loader with the same value" — the value flows from
  the resolution now.

- [ ] T2. **Loader + extractor skeletons: precedence rendering**

**Goal:** Rendered components carry the resolved channel and CloudEvent
identity; flag-less flows render exactly as today.

**Requirements:** T2, T5

**Dependencies:** T1

**Files:**
- Modify: `extractor/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl`,
  `loader/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl`
- Test: render golden cases through the template test rig for: flag path,

What is this necessary for? --set contract=Order

Because the registry resolution *deliberately doesn't own* that fact — `contract` is the transitional .NET type name (the PascalCase record in the shared-contracts project, e.g. `Order`), and nothing in the xRegistry document maps a message to it.

What each side knows:

| Value | Comes from |
|---|---|
| CloudEvent `type` | the registry (message id) → seeded by the flag |
| pubsub / topic | the registry (producer endpoint's channel) → snapshotted |
| schema (dataschema URL) | the registry (pinned default version) → snapshotted |
| `contract` (`Order`) | **you** — it names the C# type rendered from the `shared-contracts` template that the component's pipeline code consumes |

Concretely, `contract` feeds two renders: the `shared-contracts` dependency scaffolded next to the component (`loader/template.yaml` declares that dependency with `contract: '{{ .contract }}'`), and the host's `Topics.cs` (`TopicRef<Order>`, typed via the `sys create` payload). The message travels as a CloudEvent with `type: io.intropy.maxbo.product.export`; whether the payload deserializes into `Order` is a .NET-side decision the registry has no say in — that's why the CLI's seeding only touches the message parameter and the design notes keep saying "contract stays a template parameter."

So `--set contract=Order` (or answering the prompt) is the one piece of typing you still supply. If the value is annoying in practice, there are two honest escapes, neither of which is in the plan today:

1. **Template default** — give `contract` a default derived from the message (PascalCase of the last id segment, `product.export` → `ProductExport`?) — cheap, but guesses your type names and guesses wrong the moment your registry ids and C# names diverge; and since the CLI won't overwrite an existing value, you'd set it explicitly whenever the guess is wrong anyway.
2. **Make it optional for empty-body scaffolds** — when `empty: true` (the NotImplemented migration mode), the contract reference barely matters yet, so it could prompt later.

I'd leave it required until someone feels the friction for real — one `-s` flag is the price of a fact the registry genuinely doesn't have.

Now grounded in the actual branch code (the same `feat/template-library-message-wiring` commit, `767b7e5`). "MessageGraph" is really the pairing of two rendered files that give the system host its **message-dimension view**, folded into the transport view it already had.

## The two halves

**1. `Messages.cs` (the data) — rendered from `Messages.cs.tmpl`**

The system's internal message registry, emitted from the CLI's payload `messages` list — the `{name, type, contract?, dataschema?, publisher?}` entries `intropy sys create`/`sys update` assemble from components' `publishes` blocks:

```csharp
public static class Messages
{
    public static readonly IReadOnlyList<MessageDefinition> All = [ ... ];
}
```

Deliberately **internal-only**: as its doc comment says, an externally published message (one resolved from the xRegistry) has a topic here but *no* entry — the registry owns that definition, and duplicating it into the host would fork the source of truth. This is exactly the exclusion rule the CLI side enforces in `aggregateMessages` and `mergeWiring` — the template is the other half of the same contract.

**2. `MessageGraph.cs` (the transport) — a `graph` verb wrapper**

`Program.cs` routes `["graph", ..]` through `MessageGraph.Run` instead of straight to `IntropyGenerate.Run`. The reason the wrapper exists is that `Intropy.Topology` models **no messages at all** — it materializes `topics` from the components' publish/subscribe *edges* and prints the record without them. `MessageGraph` captures the backend's stdout, parses the JSON document, and injects:

```csharp
document["messagegroups"] = JsonSerializer.SerializeToNode(Messages.All, s_json);
```

…then prints the merged record. So the **MessageGraph of the system host** is: the topology record's familiar edge/transport view (components, topics, ports) plus a `messagegroups` section naming the messages the system's own components define, joined to their contract type, pinned schema, and publisher.

## The flow, end to end

```
component records (publishes blocks)
  → intropy sys create/update payload {messages: …}
    → system-host render → Messages.cs
      → dotnet run -- graph
        → IntropyGenerate prints the edge-model record
        → MessageGraph injects messagegroups
          → CLI decodes (opaque json.RawMessage) → dashboard
```

## Design notes worth knowing

- **It's plan T3's seam question, resolved as candidate (b).** The alternative was extending Intropy.Topology's model with a MessageGroup type so Generation composed the section itself; the branch chose the host-side injection — smaller, and it keeps the message-vocabulary out of the model that doesn't model messages. The trade-off to be aware of: the section's correctness lives in one template file's JSON surgery rather than a compiled model.
- **The seams are graceful by construction:** zero internal messages → no section (matching how the backend omits its own empty collections); unparseable backend output → passed through verbatim, so a failed run's diagnostics survive rather than becoming a serialization error.
- **It stays offline** — the section describes only what the workspace's records declare; the registry is never contacted at graph time.

Fixed, root cause and guard both. Summary:

## What broke

CS7003 came from a chain where the **CLI dropped a typing fact on the floor**:

1. Your loader record carries `contract: "Order"` and the external subscribe snapshot (`topic`/`pubsub` from the registry).
2. The CLI's block parser set `c.Topic` from the snapshot but **never joined the record's `contract` value into the topic wiring** — the same gap I'd fixed for the publish side, missed on the subscribe side. (Legacy flat-key records never hit it; they read `contract` directly.)
3. `sys create`/`update` payload emitted `contract: ""` for the topic → `Topics.cs` rendered `TopicRef<>` → unbound generic.

## The two fixes

**CLI (`internal/system/blocks.go`, subscribe branch)** — after the snapshot handling, the record's `contract` parameter joins the topic via soft read, exactly as the legacy parse did. Comment explains why: the block never carries the contract because it's the one typing fact the registry doesn't own. Pinned by `TestAssembleExternalSubscribeCarriesContract` (contract lands on the topic entry).

**Template (`system-host/skeleton/Topics.cs.tmpl`, on your branch, uncommitted)** — a render-time guard: a topic entry without a contract now `fail`s loudly with the remedy (set `contract` in the component's record, re-run `sys update`) instead of leaking an uncompilable host. Same fail-loudly pattern the field-collision check above it already uses.
